reviews.title: Needs NTFS Formatting Before Windows OS Will Recognize It.
reviews.comment:
This will need NTFS formatting before your Windows OS will recognize it.  It was sort of a pain on my end to go into Bios and change my load-up drives so I could format this LEVEN JPS600 2TB with Windows setup.  So far - It works well ,nice for extra space on your PC.  It’s very fast and can copy multiple large files in just a few seconds.  I’ve had it for 2 weeks and put over 1 TB of data on there so far… -  I’m not gaming or running a server, I only use it for storage.  If I was running a server I surly wouldn’t buy cheap hardware like this and expect it to perform like I just spent a million bucks.  I'm sure this may heat up and fail if you use it all the time..
Update 1 year later:  I noticed the media files quality is poor. I copied several videos to this and they play back in very poor quality. No where near as sharp and colorful as the original.

reviews.title: Do not use the included heat sink. Due to you can never take it off.
reviews.comment: I bought 2 of these drives. 1st one I pilled off the encoded heatsink and saw it had paper covering the thermopad glued in the heatsink. You will have to take the heatsink off no matter how you install it do to that. I did not use the included thermopad and heatsink due to the m.2 covers on my PC. The 2nd one I tried to use them but did not give enough space for the top screw. I tried to take the heatsink off but the glue was  needlessly to tuff to do. In doing that it tore off the 1st 2 chip which was out of warranty and I had to throw it away. Beware take the heatsink off and throw it away. You will only get one shot at installing it. However, the one I installed works great and tested great with read and write speeds.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Refused to work on two motherboards and now I'm on my third
reviews.comment:
Bought this because it was affordable and was sitting at 4.5 stars. Regret the purchase. The thing went and disappeared on my first motherboard. It was already heading out so I upgraded my pc thinking it was a thread issue. It lasted maybe two months before it again disappeared but decided to reconnect randomly. The report on the SSD showed it was dying at 80% health over 6 months after purchase. For reference, my 2tb m.2 SSD from crucial is at 96% 5 years later. So I upgraded my motherboard and it lasted maybe 3 more months before it showed issues again. Now it's once again not showing up unless I fully power down my pc and restart it. I sent out a warranty email to the company asking for a replacement, they replied 2 weeks later with info on how to spend money to send it to them in taiwan and nothing in the united states. Decided to just buy a Crucial 4TB from a company that isn't a scam.
Do not purchase. Buy from Crucial or T-Force. At least when you try to file a warranty, they don't make you jump through hoops.

reviews.title: The drive that came in this time around, was DOA.
reviews.comment:
Got the new drive this morning, except the case was empty by the look of it.
Like the unit I got last year the drive was found later at the bottom of the package.
Got it as a storage drive for my laptop, only gen3 and slow, my laptop only supports Gen 3 anyways. Not expecting much from the cheapest 4TB nvme on amazon right now. It's still faster than any SATA m.2s.
The drive came with the heat sink completely off, stuck on the package tray.
So I went to testing it out ASAP.
Pop in to my PC, crashed the system during format??!!
Computer management did detect the drive, but it never was able to format the drive, its a nvme for god's sake, formatting it should take seconds; not forever.
Put it to different nvme enclosure, the same thing happens.
This one is going back to amazon asap.
